==Notes==
*The mod's effects are only visible on Status Effects with an associated duration, either increasing the duration of the associated debuff ({{D|Puncture}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, {{D|Radiation}}, and {{D|Viral}}), or the number of ticks associated with DoT effects ({{D|Slash}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Gas}}, and {{D|Heat}}). 
**This mod will ''not'' affect the duration of crowd control effects generated by Status Effects (staggers from {{D|Impact}}, the panic duration of  {{D|Heat}}, and the stun animation caused by {{D|Electricity}}).
**However, it ''does'' affect the duration of the freeze effect applied by {{D|Cold}} after reaching 10 stacks.
**Increased Status Duration will slow down the Armor Strip effect of {{D|Heat}}. For example, with +100% status duration, the armor strip will occur every second instead of every half second. As a result, the full 50% armor strip will only be achieved after 4 seconds.
*Status Effects from the radial blasts of [[Syndicate]] [[Weapon Augments]] and Syndicate Weapons are not affected by this mod.

==Tips==
*Most useful on rifles with high [[status chance]] like the {{Weapon|Grinlok}}, {{Weapon|Miter}} and the {{Weapon|Amprex}}.

The '''Convectrix''' is a {{Faction|Corpus}} shotgun that uses two converging beams to slice enemies between them.

This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Slash}} damage.
*Innate [[multishot]] of 2 beams.
*[[Alternate Fire]] spreads the beams outward and continuously sweeps back and forth, good for covering the sides of the weapon.
*Can use the Convectrix-exclusive {{M|Efficient Beams}} mod.
*Innate {{Pol|Naramon}} polarity.

{{Advantages|class=Shotgun|
*Very high [[status chance]] per beam.
*Tied with {{Weapon|Phage}} and {{Weapon|Phantasma}} for the fastest [[fire rate]] of all shotguns.
*Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage.
*No damage falloff.
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Shotgun|
*Lowest damage of all shotguns.
*Damage ramps up from 60% (primary fire)/80% (alt-fire) to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 60%/80% over 2 seconds.
*Limited range of 30 meters.
*Does not deal full damage at the crosshair until both beams are aligned.
}}

==Acquisition==
The Convectrix's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] in the [[dojo]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*The Convectrix fires two beams with a length of 30 meters from its twin emitters, which move into position when the fire button is held. If using primary fire, the beams are emitted at the sides and then converge into the center of aim; if using secondary fire, the beams begin from the center and then diverge outwards and back again in a sweeping motion.
**The beams will deal damage to any enemies and objects caught within their length.
**Maximum beam divergence spread is affected by {{M|Tainted Shell}} and {{M|Vicious Spread}}, respectively narrowing and widening the beam's initial spread.
*The weapon's listed damage is split between the two beams, thus each beam deals half of the listed damage, per second.
**This combined with the fact that the weapon must continually contact enemies for maximum damage, means the alt fire mode consumes more ammo, and often does less damage overall.
*The most similar weapon to the Convectrix is the {{Weapon|Phage}}, an [[Infested]] continuous shotgun weapon that fires seven beams that move toward the center of the reticle when using the zoom function.
*Other similar [[Corpus]] beam weapons include:
**{{Weapon|Quanta}} and {{Weapon|Quanta Vandal}}, rifles that also fire twin continuous beams.
**{{Weapon|Flux Rifle}}, a rifle that fires a single, continuous, slash-focused beam.
**{{Weapon|Spectra}}, a secondary that fires a single, continuous, slash-focused beam.

==Tips==
*The Convectrix can use the {{M|Combustion Beam}} mod to deal damage to enemies in range upon death.
*{{M|Sinister Reach}} can be used to increase the Convectrix's range.
*Consider using {{M|Shotgun Ammo Mutation}} to help regain ammo, especially in long duration mission types.
*{{M|Vicious Spread}} has no effect at all on the beams when they are combined. While it slightly increases the radius of its sweeping pattern, the weapon converges the beams fast enough that it's not noticeable.
*The {{PAGENAME}} has a high chance of cutting corpses into pieces, making it an ideal candidate for a {{A|Desecrate}} {{WF|Nekros}} to bring along, as the game considers the cut corpses as separate entities, essentially giving multiple corpses to desecrate from a single enemy and thus yielding more chances to create more drops.
*As fire rate will not increase the speed at which the two beams converge but the ammo drain, it is ill-advised to use too many fire rate mods if you can't utilize the beams while they are not converged.
**This can be counteracted by {{M|Efficient Beams}} however.

==Trivia==
*''Convectrix'' is likely derived from the word ''convex''. A convex lens refracts multiple beams of parallel light to single focal point. This is similar to how the '''Convectrix''' works when the fire button is held, having two beams of energy converging to a single point.
*May also refer to the words ''convene'' (v. to come together) or ''converge'' (v. to tend to meet in a point or line; incline toward each other, as lines that are not parallel.) which share similar origin and meaning.
*When the beams are converged on an enemy, a singeing or burning sound can be heard, unique to the Convectrix.

Corinth Arsenal.png|Corinth as shown in the Arsenal Corinth Arsenal 2.png Corinth Arsenal 3.png File:2e75a4103fb1baafe54a1529512a2a7c.jpg {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|rDE5zzbVbRo|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|hLl-_8tEGa8|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|UzoCMoIjGGI|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|nWNhw7s3K5g|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|Uub7Mjer8nk|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|6zY3TOlnq7k|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|wJQG5pJUpko|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32.1.3}} *Fixed the Corinth using 3 rounds of ammo per alt-fire shot instead of the intended 1. {{ver|32.0.7}} *Fixed the following weapons not correctly playing their intended animations between shots: **Corinth - Fixed the slide pump playing with no sound FX {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Corinth '''Many weapons have also had their maximum ammo capacity adjusted.''' Primary Weapons: *Corinth: From 132 to 135 ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|30.5}} *Fixed shells not ejecting correctly from the Corinth while aiming. {{ver|28.0.1}} *Fixed Corinth Air Burst Alt Fire Status Chance stat UI displaying a value less than expected. {{ver|28}} *Fixed wonky Corinth reload animation after reloading and rolling at the same time. As reported here: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1168417-painful-looking-corinth-animation-bug/ {{ver|27.3.13}} *Fixed the Corinth Alt fire grenades shooting out sideways. {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. '''Condition Overload'''-type damage bonuses are a category of bonuses that are activated on transient enemy conditions, such as a [[Status Effect]] which can sometimes be applied, as opposed to an enemy [[Faction Damage Bonus|faction]] which is always applied. The current form of CO bonuses were introduced when the mod {{M|Condition Overload}} went through an iteration<ref>"Condition Overload now uses a stacking multiplier based on how many Status Effects are on the target at 120% damage per Status." - {{ver|26}} patch notes</ref> to make it additive with {{M|Pressure Point}} instead of an exponentially-scaling multiplier. Today, this same bonus is applicable to almost every weapon class, sometimes by multiple sources, but each source is categorically consistent.

;Community Terminology
*''[[CO]] (Condition Overload abbreviated. Used in this article to refer to the Condition Overload Mechanic)''
*''[[GunCO]] (Condition Overload for ranged weapons, e.g. primary and secondaries, abbreviated)''

;Writer(s) Notes
While much of this page may be considered and acknowledged by developers as bugs, this page exists to reflect the present state of the mechanic, as it has existed for multiple years, not been modified for a year, and becomes more relevant as the mechanics are utilized more by developers despite their state.
{{LatestEdit}}

==Sources of Condition Overload-Style Bonuses==
Although some sources are not related to status effects on targets, they are still based on transient conditions and are internally considered the same effect that will additively stack with each other in the list.

*{{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} (Rifle, +40% per status, stacking up to 2 times for +80% per status)
*{{M|Galvanized Shot}} (Pistol, +40% per status, stacking up to 3 times for +120% per status)
*{{M|Galvanized Savvy}} (Shotgun, +40% per status, stacking up to 2 times for +80% per status)
*{{Arcane|Secondary Shiver}} (Pistol or [[Archgun]], +45% per {{D|Freeze}} stack)
*{{Weapon|Cedo}} and {{Weapon|Cedo Prime}} (+60% per status)
*{{Resource|Dual Toxocyst Incarnon Genesis}} (+33% per status | Evolution 2, Perk 1: Carnage Reign)
*{{Resource|Lato Incarnon Genesis}} (+40% per status | Evolution 4, Perk 3: Carnage Reign)
*{{Resource|Latron Incarnon Genesis}} (+30% per status | Evolution 2, Perk 2: Swift Punishment)
*{{Resource|Angstrum Incarnon Genesis}} (+40% per status | Evolution 4, Perk 3: Fatal Affliction)
*{{Resource|Despair Incarnon Genesis}} (+40% per status | Evolution 2, Perk 1: Fatal Affliction)

*{{Resource|Soma Incarnon Genesis}} (+40% per status | Evolution 4, Perk 2: Fatal Affliction)

For example, Shiver would additively stack with {{M|Galvanized Shot}}, and {{Weapon|Dread}}'s low-HP Incarnon bonus would additively stack with the [[Shattering Frost]] decree.

{{A|Catalyze}} is not part of the category, as it breaks multiple rules such as being exponential per condition like the original pre-{{ver|26}} Condition Overload mod, and is a radial attack.

==Mechanics==
In-game, this bonus is commonly written as "+X% Direct Damage" in the EN [[localization]].

"Direct Damage" is intended language<ref>"Changed the description of Galvanized Aptitude to better reflect its current function (which clarifies that area of effect damage is not included)." - {{ver|30.9}} patch notes</ref> to specify that ''Radial Explosion Damage'' does not benefit from CO, but this is not completely true. Despite the spirit of this exclusion, many other forms of crowd damage still benefit.
*The following forms of damage apply CO:
**[[Hitscan]] - ''(e.g., {{Weapon|Braton}})''
**Hitscan Explosion - ''(e.g., {{Weapon|Trumna}} Main Fire)'' only on directly-hit target.
**Hitscan [[Ricochet]] - ''(e.g., {{Weapon|Lato}} Incarnon Form) ''
**[[Projectile]]s - ''(e.g., {{Weapon|Boltor}})''

**Beam - ''(e.g., {{Weapon|Spectra}})''
***Beam AoE - ''(e.g., {{Weapon|Glaxion Vandal}})''

**{{D|Blast}}, {{D|Electricity}} and {{D|Gas}} procs are generated based on the bonus to the initial target, but carry that proc damage to their radius.

====Math====
We can group the behaviors from the previous section into two categories based on how they stack with other damage bonuses:
*Behavior #1: "'''Multiplying'''". A multiplicative bonus that '''additively stacks''' with only CO-like damage bonuses (e.g. {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}}) AND '''multiplicatively stacks''' with other damage bonuses (e.g. {{M|Serration}}, {{A|Vex Armor}}, {{Arcane|Arcane Fury}}). Its functionality is reliable and compatible with all weapon bonuses. This is the least common way on how CO-like effects stack with damage bonuses.
**'''Base Weapon Damage {{mul}} Most Damage Bonuses {{mul}} CO {{mul}} Other Damage Multipliers'''
**Example with {{M|Serration}} and 2 procs/1 stack of {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} bonus:
***'''Final Damage = Base Weapon Damage {{mul}} (1 + {{M|Serration|1.65}}) {{mul}} (1 + {{M|Galvanized Aptitude|0.4}} + {{M|Galvanized Aptitude|0.4}})'''
<!--Mechanics below confirmed as of 2025-11-03-->
*Behavior #2/3/4: "'''Adding'''". A multiplicative bonus that '''additively stacks''' with ALL +% Damage mods, damage bonuses, AND CO-like damage bonuses (e.g. {{M|Serration}}, {{A|Vex Armor}}, {{Arcane|Arcane Fury}}, {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}}). This type is an additive recalculation of all effects, but omits +X% Damage in the recalculation, thus making CO mathematically additive to +X% Damage. However, this recalculation inadvertently omits some other effects. This is the most common way on how CO-like effects stack with damage bonuses.
**'''(Base Weapon Damage {{mul}} Most Damage Bonuses {{mul}} Other Damage Multipliers) + (Base Weapon Damage {{mul}} CO )'''
***Or '''Base Weapon Damage {{mul}} [ (Most Damage Bonuses {{mul}} Other Damage Multipliers) + CO ]'''
***Damage multipliers or effects that are ignored with Additive Stacking CO-like bonuses:
****Final Damage Multipliers
*****[[Dragon Key#Variants|Extinguished Dragon Key]]
*****[[Damage Falloff#Range Falloff|Range-based Damage Falloff]] (but not Beam ramp-up)
*****{{Arcane|Longbow Sharpshot}}
*****{{Arcane|Primary Compression}} on projectile weapons
*****{{WF|Equinox}}'s {{M|Duality}}
*****{{WF|Excalibur}}'s {{M|Furious Javelin}}
*****{{WF|Garuda}}'s [[Garuda/Abilities/Passive|Passive]]
*****{{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Eclipse}}
*****{{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Hall of Mirrors}} damage modifier
*****{{WF|Nidus}}' {{A|Parasitic Link}}
*****{{WF|Vauban}}'s {{A|Minelayer|Overdriver}}
****Base Damage increases from [[Incarnon#Genesis|Incarnon Genesis Evolutions]].
****Some Melee [[Stance]] Multipliers, on inputs with multiple hits.
****Some natural weapon stats modifiers, such as [[Bow]] charging and more.<!--
